description: Candidate tuonelang syntax spellings to compare across tokenizers. Each group poses one design question. Token metrics are ONE input to the decision, never the sole criterion — see tools/tokenizer-lab/README.md for the decision policy. Some candidates deliberately differ from the frozen v0 Constitution choice; they are kept so the trade-off that was made remains visible and reproducible.

groups.question: Which keyword introduces an executable specification?

candidates.label: test
notes: but conflates spec with conventional test frameworks

groups.question: How is the default 64-bit signed integer type spelled?

candidates.label: int
notes: lowercase; clashes with tuonelang's UpperCamelCase type convention

groups.question: How are the string/text types spelled?
How are immutable and mutable bindings introduced?

candidates.label: let-mut
notes: rejected alternative: mutability as a modifier is easy to miss/drop

groups.question: How are generic type parameters and bounds written?

candidates.label: brackets
candidates.source: fn max[T: Ord](a: T, b: T) -> T

candidates.label: angles
candidates.source: fn max<T: Ord>(a: T, b: T) -> T
notes: familiar but classic parse ambiguity with comparison/shift

candidates.label: of-keyword
candidates.source: fn max(a: T, b: T) -> T where T of Ord

groups.question: How is a name imported from a module path?

candidates.label: import-dot
notes: dot separator; familiar from many languages

groups.question: Tokens for a small but representative complete function.

candidates.label: v0-style
verbose-style
notes: longer keyword and lowercase types, for contrast

groups.question: Tokens for a representative complete program (struct, impl, function, spec).

candidates.label: v0-style
notes: frozen v0 spellings across a full small program

candidates.label: verbose-style
notes: longer keywords and lowercase types, for contrast
